newsitem.title: USA: Purchasers positive on U.S. economy - NAPM's Ore.
newsitem.headline: Purchasers positive on U.S. economy - NAPM's Ore.

text.p: The latest monthly survey by the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) reflected a stable, optimistic outlook for the U.S. economy, a NAPM executive said.
The NAPM index of manufacturing activity climbed to 53.1 in February from 52.0 in January.
"What we're seeing right now is a fairly solid economy, one that our members are optimistic about," Norbert Ore, chairman of the NAPM business survey committee, said in a teleconference.
"We see a lot of signs of growth in the manufacturing sector and (manufacturing) employment," Ore said.
But factors such as outsourcing have cut into that growth somewhat, he added.

Asked about the export orders index, which has declined somewhat over the past few months, Ore said its fate is closely tied to the performance of the dollar. "If (the dollar is) stable, that index is going to be pretty stable," he said.
